issues.failure_explanation: The abstract promises coercivity proofs for all new and key existing approximations. DDM2 is introduced as one of the two core existing approximations, yet the paper explicitly says that it cannot comment on DDM2's coercivity and gives no proof for it.

failure_location.quote: provide proofs of coercivity for all new and key existing approximations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the blanket claim with an exact list of the methods proved coercive and state explicitly that DDM2 remains without a coercivity result.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's theoretical coverage is broader in the abstract than what is actually established.
issues.title: Coercivity coverage is overstated
issues.why_classification: Only the advertised scope needs correction; no method or technical argument has to change.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated sign convention and outward normal, the closest boundary point is x-r(x)n, as also follows from x=X+r(x)n. Using x+r(x)n moves interior points farther inward and exterior points farther outward. The asserted global projection is also unique only in a sufficiently small tubular neighborhood.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x+r(x)\overline n(x) by x-r(x)\overline n(x) in both extension formulas and restrict the construction to a tubular neighborhood in which the closest-point projection is unique.
issues.overall_effect: The constructions of both data extensions use the wrong point, so the right-hand sides of all methods are not the stated normal-constant extensions as written.
issues.title: Normal extension moves away from the boundary
issues.why_classification: A forced sign correction together with the already anticipated local neighborhood restriction repairs the construction without changing the methods or analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the energy involving |nabla(phi u)|^2, while the claimed norm and the DDM1 energy involve phi|nabla u|^2. These are not identical up to epsilon scaling, and no weighted Poincare or comparison estimate is supplied to pass from one to the other.

failure_location.quote: This is identical, up to epsilon scalling, to DDM1,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restate SBM coercivity using the natural energy norm based on |nabla(phi u)|^2 plus the penalty term, and propagate that norm to thm:SBMadv, or add a proof of the missing comparison with the stated norm.
issues.overall_effect: Coercivity of SBM in the stated norm is unestablished, and the stabilized SBM advection theorem inherits this unproved diffusion coercivity.
issues.title: SBM coercivity proof establishes a different energy
issues.why_classification: A comparable energy-norm result survives, but the stated phi-gradient coercivity guarantee is weakened unless a new nontrivial estimate is added.

issues.failure_explanation: In the strong form, D multiplies both nabla(phi u) and -g nabla phi. Moving the known g-term to the right-hand side therefore gives D g nabla phi, but the method omits D. The same omission is repeated in the right-hand side of meth:mixed0adv.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor D in the first right-hand-side term of meth:mixed0 and meth:mixed0adv, and verify that the reported computations used the corrected form.
issues.overall_effect: For the explicitly considered nonconstant diffusion coefficient and nonzero boundary data, the printed MixedZ methods solve an inconsistently scaled boundary-data problem.
issues.title: MixedZ right-hand side omits the diffusion coefficient
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single coefficient already fixed by the derivation and does not change the coercivity analysis, rates, or parameter regime.

issues.failure_explanation: Let w=b·nabla phi. After factoring out phi, the preceding expression is -w+w^+=-w^-, not -1/2(w^++w^-)+w^+=1/2|w|. The displayed equality is therefore false, although the corrected expression is still nonnegative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the erroneous two-line manipulation by phi(-w+w^+)=-phi w^- and conclude nonnegativity directly.
issues.overall_effect: One step in the proof of thm:SBMadv is invalid, but the theorem's nonnegativity conclusion remains obtainable from the corrected identity.
issues.title: SBM advection proof uses an incorrect flux identity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local algebraic correction and preserves the theorem, method, and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The actual mass and divergence remainder is phi m-(1/2)phi^2 div b. Bounding it below by phi^2(m-(1/2)div b) uses phi m>=phi^2m, which requires m>=0. The stated hypothesis permits m<0 when div b<0; for example div b=-4 and m=-1 satisfy m-(1/2)div b=1, while phi m-(1/2)phi^2 div b=phi(2phi-1)<0 for phi<1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis m>=0 and insert the decomposition phi m-(1/2)phi^2 div b=phi^2(m-(1/2)div b)+phi(1-phi)m; alternatively, change the method's mass weighting from phi to phi^2.
issues.overall_effect: The stated coercivity theorem does not cover the full parameter regime allowed by eq:advCoercive, and can fail for the printed MixedO advection method.
issues.title: MixedO advection coercivity misses a sign hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A comparable theorem survives, but the least statement-level repair narrows the advertised data regime; retaining the regime requires changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: Since nabla phi approximates -delta n, the product-rule term D nabla p·nabla phi approximates -D p_N|nabla phi|. Thus the consistent equation is -div(phi D nabla p)-D p_N|nabla phi|=phi f, not the printed equation with +p_N|nabla phi| and without D.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:DDNeumann by -div(phi D nabla p)-D p_N|nabla phi|=phi f, equivalently -div(phi D nabla p)=phi f+D p_N|nabla phi|.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed diffuse formulation gives the wrong boundary forcing for a nonhomogeneous Neumann condition. The later homogeneous pressure projection is unaffected because p_N=0.
issues.title: Diffuse Neumann boundary term has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the only subsequent application is homogeneous, so all reported computations and guarantees survive.
